## Decisions
### Stay on Postgres, 4 November
- **Context:** notes grew to 2 million rows and search got slow.
- **Options:** a document store, a search service, or better indexes.
- **Chose:** Postgres with a trigram index.
- **Why:** one database to run, and the index made search 40 times faster.
- **Revisit:** at 20 million rows.

### Release every Tuesday, 2 November
- **Context:** releases slipped whenever one fix wasn't ready.
- **Chose:** ship what's ready every Tuesday.
- **Why:** small releases are easier to undo.

title: Book notes
tagline: The big idea and the lines worth keeping.
description: Send highlights as you read. Your AI keeps the quotes, the big idea and what you'll do differently.
ask: Ask which book I'm reading and what stood out so far, then start its notes.
example:
Book notes

What stuck from each book: the big idea, the lines worth keeping, and what you'll do differently. Newest book first.

## Books
### Four Thousand Weeks by Oliver Burkeman
> "The day will never arrive when you finally have everything under control." (p. 31)

- The to-do list is infinite by design. Finishing it isn't the goal.
- Pick your three big projects; everything else waits.
- Saying no to good things is the hard part.
- Rest isn't a reward for finishing: nothing is ever finished.

**The big idea:** life is short and attention is finite. Trying to do everything guarantees the important things get squeezed. Choose what to neglect, on purpose.

- [ ] Keep a list of three active projects, no more
- [ ] Do the most important thing first, before email
- [ ] Keep one evening a week with nothing planned

### Deep Work by Cal Newport
- Two focused hours beat a scattered day.
- Shallow work gets a slot of its own, so it can't leak into the rest.

**The big idea:** attention is the thing to protect. Decide when the deep work happens before the day decides for you.

title: Cornell notes
tagline: Your notes, the questions, and a summary.
description: Your notes on the right, a question for each on the left, a short summary. Then your AI quizzes you.
ask: Ask me for my lecture or reading notes, then make Cornell notes and quiz me.
example:
Cornell notes

One section per lecture or chapter. Your notes go on the right, a question that each one answers on the left, and a summary of two or three sentences closes the section. To revise, cover the right column and answer the cues.

## Lectures
### Supply and demand, 5 November
| Cue | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| What shifts the demand curve? | Income, tastes, prices of related goods, expectations. A change in the good's own price only moves along the curve. |
| What is the equilibrium price? | The price where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. |
| What does a price ceiling below equilibrium cause? | A shortage: at that price, people want more than sellers offer. |

**Summary:** Supply and demand meet at one price and quantity. Anything other than the price itself shifts a curve and moves that point; a price ceiling set too low leaves a shortage.

3. What do I want to remember?

## Entries
### Sunday 8 November
- **Today:** quiet day; finished the bookshelf and went for a long walk.
- **Energy:** low after lunch, better after coffee with Jonas.
- **Remember:** the bakery on the corner opens at seven.
- **Tomorrow:** call Mum.
### Saturday 7 November
- **Today:** helped Maja move; it went faster than we feared.
- **Energy:** the stairs took it, the pizza after gave it back.
- **Remember:** Ana said the new flat gets the evening sun.
- **Tomorrow:** reply to the landlord before noon.
